name: The Origin of Sin and the Fall

objectives.text: Identify that God made a very good world and made Adam and Eve good
Retell that Adam and Eve disobeyed God by eating the fruit He told them not to eat
Name the serpent as the one who tempted Eve to doubt what God had said
Recite the catechism answers about our first parents' fall and explain them in your own words
Describe the one command God gave Adam in the garden and the warning attached to it
Sequence the events of Genesis 3 from the serpent's question to the hiding and blaming that followed
Explain the covenant of works as the Reformed tradition describes it, including its promise of life and its threat of death
Explain that Adam and Eve were created upright yet able to sin, so the Fall came through their own free choice
Compare how Adam and Eve related to God and to each other before and immediately after their first sin
Explain Genesis 3:15 as the first promise of a Redeemer who would crush the serpent
Trace the steps of temptation in Genesis 3 and James 1 and apply them to a present-day example
Analyze the serpent's words to show how he questioned, distorted, and denied God's word
Analyze the first sin as rooted in unbelief toward God's word and a prideful desire to be like God
Explain what Scripture teaches about Satan as a fallen angel who sinned first and became the tempter of humanity
Explain why the New Testament says sin entered the world through one man even though Eve ate first
Explain how the Reformed tradition holds that God governs all things, including the Fall, yet is not the author of sin
Analyze the problem of how sin could arise in a good creature, evaluating the tradition's appeal to a changeable will and the limits of any explanation
Construct a theological summary of the Fall from a close reading of Genesis 3 in the context of Genesis 1 and 2
Evaluate interpretations that treat Genesis 3 as myth or allegory using the text's genre, genealogies, and later biblical references
Defend the historicity of Adam's fall by showing how Paul's parallel between Adam and Christ depends on it
Synthesize the Fall within Scripture's storyline from the first promise in Genesis to the removal of the curse in Revelation

changes: Removed the citation of Jude 6 and anchored Satan's fall with 2 Peter 2:4, John 8:44, 1 John 3:8 and Belgic Confession Article 12. Kept real competencies from the old list (disobedience, serpent's temptation, covenant of works, before and after comparison, temptation pattern, unbelief and pride, serpent's strategy, Satan's role, God not the author of sin, theology of Genesis 3, myth views, historicity, synthesis) and reworded them as observable student tasks. Dropped vague filler such as merely observing that sin entered a good world and folded it into a kindergarten objective on creation's goodness. Added catechism recitation, the garden command, sequencing Genesis 3, creation in uprightness with liberty to fall, Genesis 3:15 as first gospel, Adam's representative mention in Romans 5:12, and the problem of how sin arose in a good creature. Left the transmission and imputation of sin, depravity, kinds of actual sin, and the wider consequences of sin to the sibling sub-topics. Added confessional anchors including Westminster Shorter Catechism Q12 and Q13, Westminster Confession of Faith 3.1, 4.2, 5.4, 7.2 and 9.2, Heidelberg Catechism Q6 and Q7, and Belgic Confession Articles 12 and 13.
